insights.summary: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to ₹508.5 Cr with adjusted EBITDA of ₹119 Cr (23.4%) and PAT of ₹57 Cr; standalone margin was 27-28%. Huron (France) revenue was low after an accounting-method change. The MD reiterated 25-30% revenue growth for FY27, a 25% margin, more than 8,000 machines, ₹300-325 Cr from Huron and ₹2,500-3,000 Cr of order intake, with a particularly strong second half once the new 10,000-machine capacity starts.

what_changed.text: Guidance for FY27: 25-30% growth, 25% margin, 8,000+ machines, Huron ₹300-325 Cr, order intake ₹2,500-3,000 Cr

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: As a result, we expect the second half of FY27 to be particularly robust for the company.

analyst_questions.topic: Why was Q1 consolidated margin only 23%?
analyst_questions.answer: Huron revenue of about ₹35 Cr, worth about ₹20-22 Cr of margin, was not booked after a change in accounting method; it should come back in later quarters.
About ₹450 Cr for new capacity; on track.

red_flags.text: Q1 consolidated EBITDA margin (21.4% reported) is below the 25% target and depends on Huron revenue catching up.
Interest cost rose with the new capacity and is fully expensed.
Inventory is elevated ahead of the H2 ramp-up.

business_snapshot.what_they_make: CNC machine tools: entry-level to high-end turn-mill and 5-axis machines, through Jyoti and its French subsidiary Huron
business_snapshot.customers: Automotive and components, aerospace and defence, general engineering, electronics and railways
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: Q1 FY27 machines sold: 1,349 entry-level, 33 mid-range, 24 high-end
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Import substitution (about 60% of India's CNC demand is imported), defence and EV capex, capacity expansion
